title: Canna-Honey: Making Cannabis-Infused Honey at Home
h1: Canna-Honey: Infused Honey in About 20 Minutes
metaDescription: Make cannabis infused honey in about 20 minutes by whisking canna-coconut oil into warm honey, with per-tablespoon dosing math, labels and safe storage.
excerpt: Turn the canna-coconut oil you already made into honey for tea, toast and sauces, with simple math for the dose in every spoonful.
keyTakeaways: THC dissolves in fat, not water or sugar, so canna-coconut oil carries it into the honey.
Warm the honey gently, stream in the melted oil while whisking, and keep stirring as it cools.
Divide the mg in the oil by the spoonfuls of finished honey, and measure with a spoon, not a drizzle.
Refrigerate it and use within 4 days, or freeze small portions.
body:
Cannabis infused honey doesn't need a long flower infusion. If you've made canna-coconut oil, whisking it into warm honey takes about 20 minutes and turns one master infusion into a sweetener for tea, toast and sauces.

## Why the oil does the work

THC barely dissolves in water, and honey is mostly sugar and water, so flower steeped in it gives up far less THC than it would to fat. Fat dissolves THC readily. That's why this starts with canna-coconut oil, made with the jar method in our [cannabutter recipe](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/).

## Dosing: mg per tablespoon

Spread the oil's THC over the finished honey. Suppose your oil tops out around 13 mg per teaspoon: 2 tablespoons hold about 78 mg. Whisked into 1/2 cup of honey, that makes about 10 tablespoons, so roughly 8 mg per tablespoon or 2.6 mg per teaspoon. A drizzle is hard to judge, so measure it with a spoon, keep the first serving to a teaspoon or less and let at least 2 hours go by. See our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/).

## What you need

Thick, raw honey holds oil droplets better than runny honey. Add melted canna-coconut oil and, if you like, a pinch of sunflower lecithin, an emulsifier that helps the two stay blended.

## How to make cannabis infused honey

Warm the honey jar in a pan of hot water until it's runny, not hot, and melt the oil the same way. Pour the oil into the honey in a thin stream, whisking the whole time, and keep at it for a few minutes as the blend cools. If oil separates later, warm the jar and stir before measuring.

## Storage and labeling

Honey keeps well, but homemade infused oil doesn't: the CDC advises refrigerating homemade herb oils and using them within 4 days. Give the blend the same care, freezing any extra in small portions. Write the mg per teaspoon, the date and the word "infused" on every side of the jar, and store it apart from your everyday honey, up where kids and pets can't reach.

## Ways to use it

Stir a measured teaspoon into tea once it's cool enough to sip, spread it on toast or brush it over [hot honey pizza](/blog/hot-honey-pizza/). It also works in a [smoky BBQ sauce](/blog/sweet-and-smokey-bbq-sauce/) or [mulled apple cider](/blog/lifted-bright-apple-cider/). Count the teaspoons that go in, so you know the dose per serving.

faq.q: Why use coconut oil instead of infusing honey with flower?
faq.a: Because THC dissolves in fat, not in sugar or water. Steeping flower in honey extracts far less and leaves plant bits behind, while an oil infusion has already done that work. Coconut oil tastes mild, blends into warm honey easily and firms up in the fridge.

faq.q: Will the oil separate from the honey?
faq.a: It can, especially with runny honey or in a warm kitchen. Thick honey, steady whisking as it cools and a pinch of lecithin all help. If you see a layer of oil, warm the jar gently and stir before measuring, since the THC sits in the oil.

faq.q: How much canna-honey is one serving?
faq.a: Work it out from your batch, not the spoon. In the example above, a teaspoon carries about 2.6 mg at most. That sits close to the 2.5 mg ceiling Canadian public-health officials recommend for a first edible, so a level teaspoon or a little less is a sensible start.

sources.label: CDC: Botulism Prevention (homemade oils made with garlic or herbs)
University of Georgia Extension, Circular 1334: How to Safely Make Infused Oils (2024)
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)

steps: Set the honey, in a heatproof jar or bowl, in a pan of hot (not boiling) water until it loosens, about 5 minutes.
Melt the canna-coconut oil the same way and measure 2 tablespoons.
Drizzle the oil into the honey in a thin stream, whisking steadily. Add the lecithin, if using.
Keep whisking for 3 to 5 minutes as the mixture cools so the oil stays blended.
Pour into a clean jar, write the strength per teaspoon and today's date on it, and refrigerate. Use within 4 days or freeze small portions.
recipe.dosingNote: Estimate only: oil at about 13 mg per teaspoon gives 2 tablespoons roughly 78 mg. Spread through 10 tablespoons (30 teaspoons) of honey, that's about 8 mg per tablespoon, or 2.6 mg per teaspoon. That's a ceiling: your oil's actual strength hinges on the flower behind it and on what the decarb and infusion lost along the way. A teaspoon or less is plenty to start; give it at least 2 hours before any more. Mark the jar and park it beyond the reach of kids and pets.

claims.claim: THC dissolves in fat, barely in water, so canna-coconut oil carries it into honey
claims.source: PubChem CID 16078 (Solubility): 'Essentially insoluble in water', 'Soluble in fixed oils'. Read 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Honey is mostly sugar and water
claims.source: National Honey Board, Definition of Honey and Honey Products (1996, updated 2003; PDF at bjcp.org/download/honeydefs.pdf, read 2026-10-24): reducing sugars 76.75%, moisture 17.2% on average.

claims.claim: Steeping flower in honey 'pulls out very little' / 'extracts very little' (body and FAQ)
claims.fix: No measurement of honey-infusion yield was found; the solubility data support only a comparison. Now 'gives up far less THC than it would to fat' / 'extracts far less'.

claims.claim: Thick raw honey holds oil droplets better than runny honey
claims.source: Physics: droplets separate more slowly as viscosity rises (Stokes' law); a kitchen tip, not a regulated claim.

claims.claim: Sunflower lecithin is an emulsifier that helps the two stay blended
claims.source: USDA AMS technical report, Lecithin - Bleached (2009): food uses include 'emulsification'; in baking it works by 'emulsifying the fat and water'. 21 CFR 184.1400 (eCFR API, 2026-10-01): lecithin is GRAS with no limit other than good manufacturing practice.
Recipe card: 10 minutes prep plus 10 minutes cook.

claims.claim: Math: 13 mg/tsp oil x 6 tsp = 78 mg; 1/2 cup honey + 2 tbsp oil = about 10 tbsp; about 8 mg per tbsp, 2.6 mg per tsp
claims.source: Arithmetic (78/10 = 7.8; 78/30 = 2.6). 13 mg/tsp is stated as a supposition, matching the canna-butter-recipe full-cup figure.

claims.claim: 'Honey pours fast', so measure with a spoon
claims.fix: Honey is viscous; the measuring problem is that a drizzle is hard to judge. Now 'A drizzle is hard to judge, so measure it with a spoon'.
claims.source: Physical property (honey's high viscosity); the brief's point was over-pouring a drizzle.

claims.claim: A teaspoon (about 2.6 mg at most) is close to the 2.5 mg first-edible ceiling Canadian public-health officials recommend
claims.source: CCMOH statement, Public Health Agency of Canada (Jan. 6, 2020): 'Start with small amounts - 2.5 mg of THC or less'. Opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Let 2 hours go by before more (body and dosing note)
claims.fix: Now 'at least 2 hours' in both places.
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: full effects can take up to 4 hours.

claims.claim: CDC advises refrigerating homemade herb oils and using them within 4 days; freeze extras in small portions
claims.fix: UGA source added for the freezing option.
claims.source: CDC Botulism Prevention (Feb. 26, 2026): 'Refrigerate homemade oils made with garlic or herbs. Throw the oils away after 4 days.' UGA C1334 (Dec. 17, 2024): 'Alternatively, you could freeze the oil'.

claims.claim: Coconut oil tastes mild, blends into warm honey and firms up in the fridge
claims.source: Coconut oil is solid at fridge temperature: Food Chemistry: X (2026), PMC13277645, full text via Europe PMC read 2026-10-24, measured melting points of 25.25 C (77 F) for virgin and 26.86 C (80 F) for refined coconut oil.

claims.claim: If oil separates, warm and stir before measuring, since the THC sits in the oil
claims.source: PubChem solubility (THC goes with the fat phase).

claims.claim: Uses: tea once cool enough to sip, toast, hot honey pizza, BBQ sauce, mulled cider; count the teaspoons that go in
claims.source: Serving ideas; no health claim for honey or cannabis.
None stated; no shop, menu, deals or rewards links.

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 15 claims checked, 3 fixed ('pulls out very little', 'honey pours fast', wait time). The UGA freezing source was added; all cited URLs opened.
review.writerNotes: Brief suggested cupboard storage short-term; the article keeps the blend in the fridge for 4 days (or frozen) because it contains homemade infused oil, which the CDC limits to 4 days refrigerated. Oregon State Extension EM 9885 (July 2026) says properly infused honeys keep indefinitely but does not address added oils, so it is not used to extend the time. No medicinal claims for honey; no brand names.
